chapter: Life in France and Sidney Bechet
title: Never learning French
summary: Waters admits he never studied French and gets by on simple phrases and English-speaking bandmates, but can read contracts.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: OK. Before we leap forward to Germany here are a couple of things I'd like to say. How had you adapted to living in France, had you become familiar with the French language, were you scuffling?
No, I couldn't say a word, couldn't speak nothing -
How difficult was that 'cause -
(laughs), I can't speak so much now if you want to know the truth.
Had you studied any foreign language in school?
No, I never studied. And I didn't study in France, you know, I was there for years and years and didn't study a thing. I bought books, records and all kinds of things -
Well, did this make it hard for you to fend for yourself - I mean you're living in France, or did you find a lot of people spoke English and -
Yeah, I did. In the band, I mean Jacques Butler was the -
Certainly, and he spoke French -

Yeah, he spoke French. And he was the leader of the band and he had other guys that spoke English. And then I went other places, like in Germany a lot of people speak English, you know, in Switzerland same thing. In Belgium, the same thing.
How good would you say your French is now after thirty years over there?
Very bad, I'm ashamed of myself, but -

Uh huh. When you say 'very bad', would you say you have like a, the vocabulary of someone who'd only gone to school for a couple of years or a little bit more than that, or a little bit less than that -
Little bit less than that, even.
Uh huh. You mean you're just in the simple phrases category?
Benny Waters JOHP 6/16/82
Yeah. It's a shame, that's my fault.
You know how to order your food, you know how to get directions, you know how to -
Yeah, you know, things like that.
But you wouldn't, you don't read the newspaper in French.
No, that's it. And I, what makes me real bad, feel real bad - I don't understand the movies. And I [ ], I go to the movies two or three times a day when I'm not working.
As an expatriot -
And that hurts me because I could enjoy it much better. But I can read contracts now, you know, the contracts -
Uh huh -
'Cause like this contract is in French, you know -
Right, yeah, the one you showed me -
Right, I thought - because they're all the same, see.
